last_reviewed_reason: SKILL-1 wave 3 of .claude/tasks/harness-coverage-metric.md; paired with scripts/harness-coverage.py (AGG-1 wave 2). Reviewed by LEAD-B alongside the script's done-when (--format markdown + JSON, intentional_gap annotation, 60% threshold surface).

evals.prompt: Run kbg:harness-coverage and show me the 12-cell grid. I want a markdown table.
evals.expected_output: Renders the 12-cell 2x2x3 coverage grid as a markdown table with columns cell_id, status, cell_score_pct, drift_pct, intentional_gap, plus a Global rollup line (populated, holes, gaps, score, drift_30d) and a _window_sessions=30_ echo. Calls out any cell with cell_score_pct < 60% AND status != intentional_gap as a decay candidate. Names the known intentional-gap cell inf-fb-behaviour (Bockeler L465-L478 + ADR 0002 L115) so the operator knows it is not a coverage hole. Output is read-only — the skill does not write to the journal or the registry, does not emit a permissionDecision, and does not auto-fire from any hook.

assertions.name: 12_rows_present
assertions.description: Response includes a 12-row markdown table covering all 4 directions x 3 axes (comp-ff, comp-fb, inf-ff, inf-fb) x (maintainability, arch-fit, behaviour)

assertions.name: global_rollup_line
assertions.description: Response includes the Global rollup line with populated, holes, gaps, score, drift_30d counts

assertions.name: intentional_gap_named
assertions.description: Response explicitly names the inf-fb-behaviour cell as a known intentional gap (Bockeler L465-L478 + ADR 0002 L115), not a coverage hole

assertions.name: decay_threshold_called_out
assertions.description: Response calls out cells with cell_score_pct < 60% AND status != intentional_gap as decay candidates (per decay-cadence DECAY-1)

assertions.name: read_only
assertions.description: Response does not silently write to the journal, modify the registry, or emit a permissionDecision — surface is advisory only

assertions.name: 60_percent_threshold_explicit
assertions.description: Response mentions the 60% threshold from decay-cadence DECAY-1, not a different number

assertions.name: no_hook_autofire
assertions.description: Response clarifies the skill is human-triggered (kbg:harness-coverage slash command), NOT auto-fired by any hook

evals.prompt: I deleted ~/.claude/governance-events.jsonl by accident. Run kbg:harness-coverage — what does the report look like now?
evals.expected_output: Treats a missing journal as a WARNING (not an error), exits 0, and emits a 0% grid with all 12 cells in `stale` status. The known intentional-gap cell (inf-fb-behaviour) remains annotated. The operator sees a Global line: populated=0 holes=0 gaps=1 score=0% drift_30d=0%. The skill surfaces this as a valid measurement (a fresh install or a wiped journal is a known state), NOT as a hard error. The skill is read-only — it does not try to recreate the journal.

assertions.name: warning_not_error
assertions.description: Response treats the missing journal as a warning, not an error — the skill exits 0, not 1

assertions.name: zero_percent_grid_emitted
assertions.description: Response shows a 0% grid with all 12 cells in `stale` status (not `coverage_hole` — that is the registry-missing path, which is a different degradation)

assertions.name: intentional_gap_still_annotated
assertions.description: Response keeps the inf-fb-behaviour cell annotated as intentional_gap even when the journal is missing (it is a deliberate gap, not a measurement failure)

assertions.name: fresh_install_is_valid
assertions.description: Response frames a 0% grid as a *valid measurement* (e.g. fresh install, wiped journal, no fires in the window), not a coverage failure

assertions.name: read_only
assertions.description: Response does NOT try to recreate the journal — the skill is read-only and the script's degraded path is a measurement, not a write

assertions.name: global_rollup_present
assertions.description: Response shows the Global rollup line with populated=0, holes=0, gaps=1, score=0%, drift_30d=0%
